h1:
Chumphon 1-Day Itinerary
Sai Ri Beach – Sadet Tia – Seafood
intro: Most people drive straight through Chumphon on the way to Koh Tao or Koh Samui, never realizing the province itself has pretty beaches and good food — easily enough to fill a full day. This plan covers the three things first-time visitors want most: paying respects at the Sadet Tia shrine on Sai Ri Beach, taking in the Pak Nam sea views, and eating fresh seafood by the beach. We've kept the timing relaxed, and you can do it all whether you have your own car or rent a motorbike.

blocks.html: This plan takes you out to the Pak Nam Chumphon coast, about 12–20 km from the town center — an easy 20–30 minute drive. All the main stops sit along the same route, the Chumphon–Pak Nam–Sai Ri Beach road, so you can loop through them in one day without doubling back. If you arrive in Chumphon by train or bus in the morning, you can start this trip straight away.

Start the morning with a robusta coffee and breakfast in town, then head out to the coast. Late morning, honor Sadet Tia at Sai Ri Beach while the sun is still gentle. Lunch is seafood by the sea, the afternoon is the Khao Matsee viewpoint plus a walk along the fish pier, and you close out with sunset on the beach. The pacing lines up nicely with the light at each part of the day.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Morning — wake up with Chumphon coffee

items.note: Chumphon is one of Thailand's biggest robusta-growing areas. Old-school spots like Coffeebar99 roast their own beans, or try Robusta Station on Phetkasem Road (opens 07:30) for a true dark southern roast. Pair it with dim sum or a sizzling pan-egg breakfast before you head out.

items.activity: Leave town for Pak Nam – Sai Ri Beach
items.note: About 20 km, roughly 25–30 minutes. The road is good and well signed. If you don't have a car, renting a motorbike in town runs about 250–300 THB a day — the easiest option for a single day.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Late morning — Sai Ri Beach and the Sadet Tia shrine

items.activity: Honor the Krom Luang Chumphon (Sadet Tia) shrine
items.note: Set at the far end of Sai Ri Beach, this is where the Prince passed away. The shrine is built in the shape of a ship facing out to sea, and people come to ask for blessings around health and career. Open daily 07:00–17:00, no entry fee.

items.activity: See the HTMS Chumphon and the view to Koh Maphrao
items.note: Below the shrine sits a decommissioned old torpedo boat you can walk around. Looking out, you'll see Sai Ri Beach stretching off and Koh Maphrao not far offshore — the best sea-view photo angle at this spot.

Fine sand, clear water, and far fewer crowds than Hua Hin or Samui. It's a good place to sip a coconut and catch the sea breeze. If you want to swim, late morning before the sun gets harsh is the sweet spot.

blocks.title: What to know about honoring Sadet Tia
blocks.html: Paying respects to Sadet Tia comes with its own customs — by local belief, people offer betel nut, cigarettes, and bananas. If you didn't bring any, there are vendors selling offerings in front of the shrine. Dressing modestly suits the place better.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Chumphon trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Chumphon
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Lunch — a seafood meal by the sea

blocks.html: Pak Nam Chumphon is a fishing town, so the seafood here is fresher and better priced than in the big tourist destinations. Most restaurants sit right on the water or near the fish pier, taking their catch straight from local boats. We've picked places that are genuinely open and that locals actually eat at, so you can choose by location and style.

items.name: Krua Je Ang
items.blurb: A well-known Pak Nam Chumphon seafood spot, right across from Novotel Chumphon Beach. Fresh catch from local boats, with grilled prawns, fried fish, and fish-roe sour curry among the most-ordered dishes. Breezy seaside setting.

items.name: Mae Mai Seafood
items.blurb: A beachside seafood place that draws plenty of stops along the Chumphon–Pak Nam road. The prawns are big and as fresh as if they came straight off the boat. Known for oysters, horseshoe-crab roe salad, and steamed crab claws — and the prices aren't steep.

items.name: Chaloem Chill-Lay
items.blurb: A seaside spot on Sai Ri Beach with a relaxed, breezy beach vibe — good for dinner. Standout dishes are the hot-pot steamed egg, stir-fried clam muscle, and garlic-fried mackerel.
items.meta: Open 16:00–22:00 · closed Mondays · Sai Ri Beach

items.name: Baan Khun Ta
items.blurb: A Sai Ri Beach spot people photograph for social media often. The signature dishes are Ryukyu fish-roe salad, prawns in fish sauce, tamarind-sauce prawns, and a mixed grilled-seafood platter.

items.name: Nong Mai Sai Ri Beach Resort
items.blurb: A seaside seafood restaurant inside a resort on Sai Ri Beach, open from morning through evening. Good if you want to settle in for a long beachfront meal at any time of day.

items.name: Eateries by the Pak Nam fish pier
items.blurb: The fish-pier zone has several made-to-order seafood stalls. Everything is fresh and cheap because it's right where the catch comes in — a good fit for budget travelers who want fresh seafood at genuine local prices.

blocks.title: Ordering seafood the smart way
blocks.html: Always ask the per-kilo price before ordering prawns or crab, since it's charged by weight and varies with the season. During the months when the bay is closed to fishing, some items may be in shorter supply. The dishes nearly every restaurant does well are grilled prawns, steamed squid with lime, and fish-roe sour curry.

blocks.text: Afternoon — the viewpoint and the fish pier

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Afternoon — looking down on the Pak Nam coast

items.activity: Head up to the Khao Matsee viewpoint
items.note: Drive about 800 meters up the hill to the viewpoint for a 360-degree view of the Pak Nam community, Phradon Phap Beach, Sai Ri Beach, and the islands. At the top there's the Tham Sing coffee cafe where you can sip a coffee and watch the sea.

items.activity: Walk the Pak Nam Chumphon fish pier
items.note: Watch the fishing life and the boats coming in. There's fresh seafood for sale at low prices, and if you want to pick up dried squid or shrimp paste to take home as gifts, this is the place.

A long beach running parallel to the road, with white sand and clear water — a pleasant drive with plenty of spots to pull over for photos. It's quieter than Sai Ri Beach, good for finding a calm corner to catch the breeze.

blocks.text: Evening — close out with the sunset

blocks.html: The Pak Nam coast faces the right way to catch lovely evening light — between 17:30 and 18:30 the sky shifts color over the sea. You can sit at a beachfront spot like Chaloem Chill-Lay, order dinner, and wait for the light, or just settle back on Sai Ri Beach. If you need to catch a train back to Bangkok or head on to Koh Tao, allow about 30 minutes to get back into town.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Evening — catch the last light, then head back to town

items.activity: Watch the sunset on Sai Ri or Phradon Phap Beach
items.note: Grab a chair at a beachside spot or lay out a mat on the sand. The breeze is pleasant, it's not crowded, and it's the quietest, prettiest stretch of the day.
If you're still hungry, settle in at a seaside spot for dinner, or head back into town to wander the evening market and catch an evening train or bus right on time.

blocks.text: Adjust the plan to the time you have

items: Only a morning — focus on honoring Sadet Tia, walking Sai Ri Beach, then lunch seafood at Krua Je Ang or Mae Mai. That covers the highlights.
Only an afternoon — start at Khao Matsee in the afternoon, drop down to honor Sadet Tia, walk the fish pier, then wait for the evening light on the beach.
Traveling with kids or older relatives — cut the hill walking, focus on Sai Ri Beach and Khao Matsee (you can drive up), and pick places with shaded seating like Nong Mai or Krua Je Ang.
Continuing to the islands — Chumphon is the gateway to Koh Tao, with ferries from the pier. Make this a rest day before catching the morning boat the next day.
From Chumphon town, Sai Ri Beach is about 20 km, a 25–30 minute drive, paved the whole way.
No car? Rent a motorbike in town for about 250–300 THB/day — the most flexible way to do a single day.
Arriving by train or bus, get off at Chumphon station and rent a vehicle or hire a ride from there, since all the sights are outside the town.
Parking at the Sadet Tia shrine, Khao Matsee, and the beachside restaurants is free. On long weekends it gets busy, so aim to go in the morning.

faq.q: What can you do in Chumphon in one day?
faq.a: A route that works well is honoring the Sadet Tia shrine on Sai Ri Beach in the late morning, seafood by the sea at lunch, the Khao Matsee viewpoint and a walk along the Pak Nam fish pier in the afternoon, then sunset on the beach to close out. All the stops sit along the same route, so you can loop through them comfortably in a single day.

faq.q: Is Sai Ri Beach far from Chumphon town?
faq.a: Not far — about 20 km from town, roughly a 25–30 minute drive, paved the whole way and well signed. If you don't have a car, renting a motorbike in town for about 250–300 THB a day makes getting around easy.

faq.q: What time does the Sadet Tia shrine open, and what should I bring to make an offering?
faq.a: The Krom Luang Chumphon shrine is open daily 07:00–17:00 with no entry fee. By local belief, people offer betel nut, cigarettes, and bananas. If you didn't bring any, there are vendors selling offerings in front of the shrine. Dressing modestly suits the place.

faq.q: Which seafood restaurants in Chumphon are good?
faq.a: Locals often go to Krua Je Ang and Mae Mai Seafood around Pak Nam. On Sai Ri Beach there's Chaloem Chill-Lay, Baan Khun Ta, and Nong Mai Sai Ri Beach. The dishes nearly every place does well are grilled prawns, steamed squid with lime, and fish-roe sour curry.

faq.q: Which part of the day suits which spot best?
faq.a: Morning is best for honoring Sadet Tia and walking the beach before the sun gets harsh, lunch is seafood by the sea, the afternoon is Khao Matsee for the 360-degree view, and 17:30–18:30 in the evening is when the sunset turns the sky beautiful colors over the Pak Nam coast.
